# TruncAI-OTiX

> Public D0 overview of an internally executable, local, synthetic and non-operational technical reference for bounded AI decision support, traceability and controlled technical evaluation.

Canonical website: https://truncaiotix.com/
Official public repository: https://github.com/truncai-otix/TruncAI-OTiX-public
Language: English
Contact: contact@truncaiotix.com

## Primary public pages

- What is TruncAI-OTiX?: https://truncaiotix.com/what-is-truncai-otix/
- Evidence and verification boundary: https://truncaiotix.com/evidence/
- High-level architecture: https://truncaiotix.com/architecture/
- Capability boundary C0-C4: https://truncaiotix.com/capability-boundary/
- Evaluation path and limitations: https://truncaiotix.com/evaluation/
- Frequently asked questions: https://truncaiotix.com/faq/

## Public access and crawler policy

- The canonical website, these topic pages and this summary are public D0 material.
- Search and user-request crawlers are intentionally permitted by robots.txt, including OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Googlebot and Bingbot.
- Separate model-training or model-improvement crawlers are blocked where a dedicated robots token exists, including GPTBot, ClaudeBot and Google-Extended.
- The official public repository contains approved D0 website sources, README and publication history: https://github.com/truncai-otix/TruncAI-OTiX-public
- Public textual content is designed to be retrievable without authentication, cookies or client-side JavaScript.
- Technical source and evaluation artefacts are not public; approved evaluators may receive a scoped controlled package only under explicit authorisation and appropriate confidentiality terms.

## Current baseline

- Version: V2.1.
- Status: internally executable transferable baseline with explicit limitations.
- Environment: local, synthetic and non-operational.
- Maximum authorised capability: C2 RECOMMEND.
- Prohibited capabilities: C3 PREPARE / ISSUE and C4 EXECUTE / CONTROL.
- Human decisions occur outside the advisory runtime.

## Evidence components

- Evidence Spine: versioned, integrity-linked records supporting traceability and replay within the tested scope.
- Agent Governance: identity, human ownership, purpose and tool binding, minimum privilege, validity, budgets, revocation and HITL escalation.
- Assurance Lab: deterministic synthetic evaluation campaigns, negative testing, tamper detection and replay.
- Baseline Closure: closure and fail-closed checks against silent expansion of authority, validation scope or claims.

## Internal verification snapshot

- Evidence Spine: 40/40 INTERNAL PASS.
- Agent Governance: 26/26 INTERNAL PASS.
- Assurance Lab: 30/30 INTERNAL PASS.
- Baseline Closure: 17/17 INTERNAL PASS.
- Additive total: 113/113 internal tests for the recorded object, fixtures, version and environment.
- Assurance Lab reports a deterministic campaign of 10,000 virtual synthetic cases; this is not real-world operating history.
- Industrial continuity evidence: INCONCLUSIVE and not counted as PASS.
- Real human-review evidence: INCONCLUSIVE and not counted as PASS.

## Applied evidence path

- Energy is the only current domain with project-specific applied evidence.
- The frozen V2.0 Energy Advisory demonstrator is local, read-only and consultative.
- It analyses historical telemetry and provides advisory output for human consideration.
- It does not control inverters, batteries, protections, grid, loads or other operational assets.
- Private real-energy data is excluded from public disclosure.
- Railway and other sector applications remain transfer hypotheses and have not been validated.

## Claim boundary

- No external or industrial validation is claimed.
- No certification, regulatory conformity or production readiness is claimed.
- No absolute security, complete threat coverage or functional safety is claimed.
- No proven cost, energy, emissions, forecasting or anomaly-detection benefit is claimed.
- Potential regulatory relevance depends on intended purpose, classification, actor role and deployment context and requires competent external legal and sectoral assessment.

## Evaluation

The progressive path is public overview, scoped technical review, synthetic clean-room evaluation, confidential review and—only when justified and authorised—evaluation with third-party data. Portability to a third party's real environment has not yet been demonstrated.
